In this tree, Denisova 3 is the only included Denisovan individual, while ZKD, SJD14M, HX-S1, HX-S2, SJD10A and SJD10M refer to H. erectus specimens studied previously. b, Amino acid occupancy for reference great ape specimens, including extinct and extant hominins, for three selected dental enamel protein positions relevant for the five Naxian and Baxian hominin specimens studied proteomically in this study. c, Selected peptide-spectrum matches showing coverage of the H. erectus-derived AMBN-253G substitution observed in four of the Naxian and Baxian hominins. Peptide fragment ion series extracted from PEAKS Online v.12.

Although individual variation in protein amino acid sequences can exist between individuals, we find, among the regions of the proteins covered in our ancient data, only a single position with sequence variation among the worldwide distributed modern humans included in our database search (Table 1). In general, among extant hominids, out of the 43 amino acid positions variable among and between great ape individuals included, and in cases in which we have coverage for at least one of the four hominins studied here, only five positions contain sequence heterogeneity between the included individuals where at least four or more individuals of a single genus share variation (one position in H. sapiens, three in the genus Pan and one in the genus Pongo; Table 1). Notably, the four teeth carrying the derived AMBN A253G substitution shared with the previously reported H. erectus specimens from Zhoukoudian, Sunjiadon and Hexian differ from those six specimens, as the Naxian and Baxian hominins do not carry the derived AMBN M273V substitution (Table 1, Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 3). Thus, the observation of the AMBN Gly253 substitution combined with the observation at AMBN Met273 in four hominin teeth, of at least three individuals, if the two M1s from Naxian cave represent the same individual, from two late Middle Pleistocene sites suggests that the hominin population to which they collectively belonged has not previously been sampled using molecular methods, either genetic or proteomic.

To further explore the phylogenetic placement of the Naxian and Baxian specimens, we conducted a Bayesian phylogenetic analysis. Note that, owing to the sparseness of dental enamel proteomic data, such analyses in palaeoproteomics generally have to assume that there has been no recent gene flow between the individuals and populations included in the analysis. We find that the four Naxian and Baxian individuals with the AMBN A253G substitution cluster together in a clade outside the branch of previously reported Denisovans, Neanderthals and modern humans (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Figs. 4 and 5). The topology of the clade formed by Denisovans, Neanderthals and modern humans matches the expected configuration in the main analysis, albeit with low internal node support (Fig. 4). The topology of these three hominin populations changes once additional modern human and great ape individuals are added to the phylogenetic analysis (Extended Data Figs. 4 and 5). The expected topology of this clade is challenging to obtain when using proteomic data from dental enamel proteins, as reported previously29,39,40, and it is evidenced by the low support value of this clade in our analyses (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Figs. 4–6). Nevertheless, the values supporting the nodes for the remaining branches, including the one placing the Naxian and Baxian specimens as an outgroup to the other hominins, are high in all analyses (>0.995). The Naxian and Baxian individuals are placed in a clade together with six previously reported H. erectus specimens. Those six specimens are placed together with strong support and separate from the four Naxian and Baxian individuals carrying the AMBN A253G substitution (Fig. 4). This strengthens the notion that these four Naxian and Baxian cave specimens represent a H. erectus hominin population that has not been sampled molecularly before. Furthermore, the phylogenetic analysis suggests that, although based on sparse data, this hominin population might have diverged before the divergence of the common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals and Denisovans. These phylogenetic observations are in accordance with the morphological analysis of these specimens, strengthening the case that these specimens belong to a previously unsampled lineage of H. erectus.

By contrast, proteomic analysis of PA1796 from Baxian cave reveals that this specimen does not contain the derived AMBN A253G amino acid substitution (Extended Data Fig. 6b). It has no uniquely derived substitutions compared to the other four teeth, nor does it share uniquely derived amino acid substitutions with the Denisovan, Neanderthal or modern human individuals present in our reference panel (Table 1). Phylogenetic analysis of this specimen places it outside of the H. erectus clade, with varying topologies with low support in relation to its placement in relation to archaic hominins (Denisovans and Neanderthals) or the clade including Neanderthals, Denisovans and modern humans (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 6a). The protein sequences reconstructed for this tooth are therefore different from the other four specimens studied proteomically, mirroring the morphological analysis that also indicates this specimen represents a taxon other than H. erectus. Only a single Denisovan genomic reference is currently available, the D3 specimen from Denisova cave, Russia, implying that our understanding of protein sequence polymorphisms for Denisovans is by definition limited. Future morphological and genomic or proteomic research on hominin teeth from the region could provide additional frameworks to allow more precise taxonomic classification of PA1796 into a non-erectus group, representing either southern Asian representatives of Denisovans (H. longi) or potentially another population or species.

Eight of the late Middle Pleistocene Homo teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves exhibit metric and morphological features that lie within the range of East and Southeast Asian H. erectus and that differ from those of Denisovans (H. longi), Neanderthals (H. neanderthalensis), or Pleistocene and Holocene modern humans (H. sapiens). The palaeoproteomic evidence provides further confirmation that four of these teeth indeed fall outside of the known genetic and proteomic sequence variation of H. neanderthalensis, H. longi and H. sapiens, but are consistent with a H. erectus-derived substitution recently described for Chinese specimens dating to around 0.4 Ma (ref. 13). The recovered proteomic evidence is therefore compatible with the morphological data. Dated to between 324 and 184 ka (ref. 12), these H. erectus teeth substantially extend the known temporal range of H. erectus fossils on the Asian mainland, bringing the extent of the mainland H. erectus fossil record closer to the latest known Javanese H. erectus, dated to 117–108 ka (ref. 8). The recovery of a unique proteomic signature of mainland H. erectus from the Middle Pleistocene of East Asia furthermore suggests that specimens attributed to this species could harbour several hominin populations13, and make it possible to molecularly test whether other H. erectus fossils from the region that could potentially date to the late Middle Pleistocene, such as those from Changyang cave (Hubei province, China)11,22 and Chaoxian cave (Anhui Province, China)23, also represent specimens belonging to the same mainland H. erectus hominin population, or whether they have a proteomic signature more similar to earlier H. erectus13.

The discovery of the Naxian and Baxian H. erectus specimens in the late Middle Pleistocene of southern East Asia enriches the hominin occupation scenario in the region. A Denisovan mandible has been described from the Penghu channel off the coast of Taiwan, dating to either 190–130 or 70–10 ka (refs. 7,48). In Laos, based on morphological analysis, a Denisovan molar has been described from Tam Ngu Hao 2, dating to between 163 and 131 ka (ref. 6). Genetic evidence on the timing of Denisovan introgression into the genomes of living humans also suggests that Denisovans were present in East and/or Southeast Asia well into the Late Pleistocene1,49. Moreover, several craniodental remains, such as Harbin, Penghu 1 and Xiahe 1, were identified molecularly as H. longi (Denisovans)7,9,17,19, and several other late Middle Pleistocene specimens probably belong to this population as well (for example, Xujiayao and Hualongdong), including also some non-erectus fossils from southern Asia (for example, Maba, Narmada, TNH2-1)6,50. It therefore seems plausible that the H. erectus population represented by the fossils from Naxian and Baxian cave on the mainland existed in relatively close proximity to Denisovan hominins.

Even though the geometric morphometric analysis of the EDJ suggest that the PA1796 M2 retains plesiomorphic aspects (mostly due to the short EDJ height), the specimen also differs from the morphology of the comparative H. erectus sample (Supplementary Note 2). The lack of a comparative sample for Denisovans (H. longi) represents a substantial bias in our ability to morphologically identify them. The non-metric morphology of PA1796 differs markedly from that of Chinese H. erectus by the lack of wrinkling on the EDJ, the absence of accessory fossae, the relatively large talon and the lingually shifted hypocone25,26 (Supplementary Notes 1 and 2). Moreover, the palaeoproteomic analysis of PA1796 demonstrates a different signal compared to the other Baxian and Naxian specimens, as well as to the six H. erectus teeth from Zhoukoudian, Hexian and Sunjiadong13 (Fig. 4), strongly suggesting the presence of a hominin population other than H. erectus in Baxian cave. However, among the protein sequences available to us now, the PA1796 specimen does not exhibit the known proteomic variation associated with Denisovans, although it should be acknowledged that only a single Denisovan reference genome is currently available. PA1796 could therefore either represent a still-unrecognized H. erectus group that would differ in molecular and morphological aspects from the currently known H. erectus specimens, a hypothesis that we consider unlikely (Supplementary Note 2) but cannot outright reject, or belong to a non-erectus group, possibly related to H. longi. Future morphological and proteomic research on hominin teeth from the region, as well as the availability of a growing number of Denisovan genomes and proteomes, could therefore provide additional frameworks to allow a more precise classification of the PA1796 specimen.

Recent findings suggest that the H. erectus specimens from Baxian and Naxian caves extend the geographical and temporal extent of mainland Asian H. erectus well into the late Middle Pleistocene. Occupying rainforest environments12, these H. erectus populations probably co-existed in close spatial and temporal proximity to southern Asian Denisovans. Mainland Southeast Asia therefore appears as a key region to study the evolution, genetics and archaeologically visible behaviours of multiple sympatric hominin species.

Sources indicate that the Baxian and Naxian hominin specimens were scanned using X-ray microtomography using the 225 kV micro-computed tomography scanner at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP, Beijing, China) according to the following parameters: 140 kV voltage, 120 µA, 0.5 angular increment one step and 360° of rotation. The final volumes were reconstructed with isotropic voxel sizes of 15.7–32.0 µm. A semi-automatic threshold-based segmentation was carried out in Avizo v.7.1 (FEI Visualization Sciences Group) and a volumetric reconstruction was then generated for each specimen. A full morphological description of each tooth can be found in Supplementary Note 1.

According to recent reports, dental surface models were imported in Geomagic Design v. X 64 (3D Systems, Rock Hill) to separate the crown from the tooth roots. The crown and roots were digitally isolated at the cervix using the cervix-best-fit plane as a reference51. Five variables were then measured or calculated: (1) Ve, the volume of the enamel cap (mm3); (2) SEDJ, the surface area of the EDJ (mm2); (3) Vcdp, the volume of the crown dentine and pulp (mm3); (4) 3DAET, 3D average enamel thickness (Ve/SEDJ; mm)52; (5) 3DRED, the ratio of 3D average enamel thickness to 3D average dentine thickness (Ve1/3/Vcdp1/3 × 10)53.

Diffeomorphic surface matching was applied to analyse the EDJ shape of the least worn teeth from Baxian and Naxian caves (methodological details are provided in Supplementary Note 2). This landmark-free, mesh-based approach was previously demonstrated to efficiently distinguish the EDJ of various hominin species6,22,27. Owing to occlusal wear, the apex of the dentine horns of some of the specimens had to be reconstructed before the analysis (Supplementary Note 2 and Supplementary Figs. 18 and 21). We first confirmed that the EDJ of the Baxian and Naxian specimens differed from that of Pongo and belonged to Homo (which was also confirmed independently by palaeoproteomics). We then compared the Baxian and Naxian EDJs to those of H. erectus s.l., H. neanderthalensis, H. longi and H. sapiens. The H. erectus sample includes dental remains from African and Asia that are regarded by some as belonging to H. ergaster and H. erectus s.s. (Supplementary Table 3). We indicated the labels of the H. erectus specimens in Fig. 2 to show the distribution of the African and Asian material in the morphospace. Canonical variate analyses were conducted and the Baxian and Naxian specimens, as well as the Denisovan molar from Tam Ngu Hao 2 (ref. 6), were projected a posteriori into the canonical variate analysis morphospace. Typicality probabilities were computed for the Naxian and Baxian teeth to provide a quantitative estimation of their most likely taxonomic attribution.

In a recent development, for Naxian cave, fauna and hominin specimens were sampled using a handheld drill with a diamond-tipped drill bit, resulting in between 10 mg and 97 mg of powder for the faunal samples and up to 6 mg of hominin dental enamel. For Baxian cave, dentine was obtained using a handheld drill (36.5 and 43.2 mg of powder), while the dental enamel was sampled using an acid etch. All sampling and extraction steps were conducted in ancient molecular laboratories regularly used for ancient DNA and/or ancient protein analysis, including standard procedures to prevent contamination from occurring in the sampling and extraction environments, including wearing full body suits, hairnets, multiple layers of nitrile gloves, footies and positive air pressure.

According to recent reports, dental enamel extracts for Naxian cave were generated using 5% HCl, following previously published protocols31,54. Likewise, dental enamel extracts from the acid etching of the Baxian cave specimens followed previously published protocols54. The dentine samples of fauna from Naxian cave were extracted using a variant on previously published EDTA-based protocols55. For Baxian cave, the hominin dentine extractions followed a HCl-based protocol commonly used for ZooMS analysis, but with modifications to separate protein fragments by size9,56. Full protein extraction protocols are provided in Supplementary Note 3.

It has been revealed that faunal extracts from Naxian cave were separated on the EASY-nLC 1200 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) system coupled to a Exploris 480 Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Hominin dental enamel extracts from Naxian cave were analysed on the Vanquish Neo UPLC (Thermo Fisher Scientific) system coupled to a Exploris 480 Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Dentine extracts from Baxian cave were first analysed on the Bruker Autoflex MaX MALDI-ToF MS instrument. Subsequent to the detection of collagen peptides, both the dentine and the dental enamel extracts from Baxian cave were analysed on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Easy n-LC 1200 HPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) over a 120 min gradient. Blank extractions were included in all cases to monitor the existence of exogenous contaminants during the procedure.

Recent findings suggest that raw data files were searched separately by tissue type and cave site, using PEAKS, pFind and MaxQuant in parallel. Initial searches in PEAKS revealed the possibility of a unique substitution in AMBN, while PEAKS and pFind informed on the composition of post-translational modifications (PTMs) that should be taken into account. After initial searches, final searches using an updated protein sequence database and updated PTM information for dental enamel and the full human proteome for dentine were performed (further details are provided in Supplementary Note 3).

Protein deamidation was calculated according to a previous study for MaxQuant data57. Other PTM ratio analyses were conducted by peptide-spectrum match spectral counts or peptide counts, unless indicated differently (applying to MaxQuant, pFind and/or PEAKS). Unipept analysis was carried out using all peptide matches against endogenous, dental-enamel-specific proteins58. As described above, a project-specific database was used for data analysis that includes protein sequence variation beyond that available within UniProt. As a result, Unipept analysis will not be able to match all peptides to the same taxonomic level as the one present in the protein sequence database used. Sequence reconstruction was performed for pFind, PEAKS and MaxQuant data jointly, resulting in a single protein sequence reconstruction for each specimen. Specifically, sequences from different search engines were overlaid for each specimen to generate a single protein consensus sequence. Amino acid positions where PEAKS, pFind and MaxQuant disagreed with each other were not called, and reversed to ‘X’. Positions possibly phylogenetically informative were manually inspected, fragment ion series were checked and E values were assessed. Where necessary, positions potentially introducing invalid sequences were subsequently removed from the protein sequence reconstructions. The consensus sequences were subsequently aligned to a subset of the PaleoProPhyler database of hominid dental enamel sequences, which included four individuals from each of the genera Pongo, Gorilla and Pan, as well as three Neanderthals41,42,43, one Denisovan44 and three present-day H. sapiens from the sub-Saharan Yoruba population. We also added the dental enamel protein sequences for Homo antecessor29 and Penghu 1 (ref. 7) (a Denisovan individual) and carried out Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of the Naxian–Baxian individuals using a combination of different proteins for each tree. The combinations are indicated in each figure (Extended Data Figs. 4–6 and Supplementary Figs. 33–43). The available H. erectus protein sequences from a single specimen (D4163) from Dmanisi, Georgia, were not included in the phylogenetic analysis carried out here because the phylogenetic position of the specimen could not be resolved in the original study29.

These fossils and their CT data are freely available to access for any researchers. Roberto De Zerbi speaks out on ‘unlucky’ Savio injury in Tottenham’s Ipswich win

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham winger Savio returned from injury on Saturday and almost immediately suffered the same injury that had just kept him out for six weeks.
  • Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in north London, thanks to goals from teenager Luca Williams-Barnett on his first Premier League start and Dominic Solanke.
  • Tottenham climbed to ninth with the win, but there was disappointing news for them as Savio came off the bench in the second half but did not make the final whistle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham winger Savio returned from injury on Saturday and almost immediately suffered the same injury that had just kept him out for six weeks.

Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in north London, thanks to goals from teenager Luca Williams-Barnett on his first Premier League start and Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham climbed to ninth with the win, but there was disappointing news for them as Savio came off the bench in the second half but did not make the final whistle.

The summer-signing from Manchester City had not played since the draw with Manchester United on October 10 and may now face a similar period on the sidelines after a recurrence of the same hamstring problem.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi mentioned: ‘I’m sorry for Savio’s injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him.

According to recent reports, ‘He’s a crucial player for us. He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season.’.

The 22-year-old joined from Manchester City for an initial £75 million and scored on his debut in a League Cup win over Charlton Athletic, but has not done much of note since then, hampered by injury.

The emergence of Williams-Barnett is much better news for De Zerbi, who has not been shy in talking up the talents of the 18-year-old who has come through the youth ranks at Spurs.

‘Luca is a special player,’ noted the Italian. ‘I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He’s lucky because he’s playing in a top club with top team-mates.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be key.

Industry observers note that ‘The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

‘And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

‘Even if they are Ballon d’Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.’.

De Zerbi, who was serving a touchline suspension against Ipswich, was asked if Williams-Barnett could reach the levels of the superstars he mentioned and remarked: ‘Yes, I think so.

‘And one of the best things in my career… I’ve seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

Sources indicate that ‘I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?’.

Spurs have now won four of their last five Premier League games and ended Saturday just three points adrift of Bournemouth in fourth.

Harry Kane injury could force Bayern Munich into £44m transfer dilemma amid Arsenal, Man United interest

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39.
  • Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.
  • The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39.

Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.

The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

In a recent development, the 33-year-old was withdrawn after just 20 minutes, leaving Vincent Kompany without his first-choice centre-forward at a crucial stage of the campaign. The setback is particularly concerning given Bayern's limited options in the position and their demanding domestic and European schedule.

One player who could now become increasingly relevant to the German club's recruitment discussions is Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who has been monitored by Bayern scouts in recent weeks.

However, the 22-year-old's reported valuation of up to €50m (£44m), combined with Brugge's reluctance to sanction a winter departure, presents a significant obstacle should Bayern decide to bring forward their search for attacking reinforcements.

According to German newspaper TZ, Bayern have sent scouts to Belgium on several occasions to monitor Tresoldi, whose performances have attracted considerable attention across Europe.

The Germany Under-21 international has scored 14 goals and provided one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as one of the most productive young forwards on the continent.

His form has inevitably generated transfer speculation, with reports suggesting that Bayern view him as a potential long-term addition to their attacking department.

Significantly, the club's interest emerged before Kane suffered his injury against Koln.

Earlier this month, Bayern were reportedly exploring the possibility of signing Tresoldi as an additional attacking option despite having recently extended Kane's contract until 2029. The idea was to strengthen their squad with a younger centre-forward capable of developing alongside the England international.

That strategy could now face an unexpected test.

With Kane unavailable for several months, Bayern must decide whether their existing attacking resources can compensate for his absence or whether an immediate signing would provide greater security.

Tresoldi possesses several attributes that could appeal to Kompany, including his movement inside the penalty area, ability to attack space behind defenders and increasingly reliable finishing.

However, securing his signature midway through the campaign would be far from straightforward.

Reports in Belgium have indicated that Club Brugge are determined to retain the striker until at least the summer, with the club's hierarchy reluctant to entertain offers during the January transfer window.

According to Het Nieuwsblad, Brugge have made their position clear to interested clubs, although an exceptional financial proposal could potentially force a reassessment.

German reports have placed Tresoldi's potential price between €40m (£35m) and €50m (£44m), with the forward under contract until June 2029.

Bayern have not submitted a confirmed offer, and there is currently no evidence that Kane's injury has prompted formal negotiations with the Belgian club.

Any attempt to accelerate a move for Tresoldi could also bring Bayern into competition with several Premier League clubs.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with the Club Brugge striker, whose impressive scoring record has strengthened his reputation as one of Europe's most promising young centre-forwards.

That timeline broadly aligned with Bayern's previous interest, which appeared to concern the longer-term development of their attacking squad rather than an urgent winter acquisition.

Kane's injury introduces a potentially vital difference in Bayern's circumstances, although it does not establish that the Bundesliga champions have changed their transfer strategy.

The club must also assess whether investing heavily in another centre-forward would make sense once Kane returns to fitness, particularly after committing to a upcoming long-term agreement with their leading goalscorer.

Kompany has alternatives within his squad, but none offers the same combination of finishing, creativity and experience as the England captain.

A temporary tactical adjustment may therefore be necessary, with greater responsibility potentially falling on Bayern's other attacking players.

The German champions could also turn to their academy, where 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention following impressive performances for the youth teams.

According to Kicker, the teenager was already under consideration for greater involvement with the senior squad before Kane's injury, although expecting him to replace the England international immediately would represent a considerable leap.

For Bayern, the dilemma is therefore as much about timing as identifying the right player.

Tresoldi was already an attractive prospect before Kane's setback, but Brugge's reported resistance to a January sale means that accelerating the deal could prove expensive and difficult.

Meanwhile, Arsenal and Manchester United remain interested parties whose own plans have been linked to the summer window.

Bayern's next decision will depend on whether Kompany believes his squad can absorb Kane's absence or whether the club considers an early investment necessary to protect its ambitions in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany.
  • Recent findings suggest that they only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow.
  • In a recent development, the scientists see the work as critical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany. Keeping the roots intact, conservationists carefully lift shoots from a donor meadow of seagrass and place them in a bag.

Recent findings suggest that they only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow. They've already picked out a prime area for the young plants, which need sandy sediment, shelter from waves and currents and sufficient light and oxygen to thrive.

In a recent development, the scientists see the work as critical. Myriam Spicka, who heads the NGO Seagrass Conservation, notes she has "seen the changes" in the more than 30 years she's been diving. And she is not the only one who has witnessed the destruction.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Scientists estimate that around 60% of the Baltic coast's seagrass meadows have disappeared.

"That's the bad news," said marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch from the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel . "The good news is that the decline has stopped.".

In a recent development, underwater seagrass meadows feed and shelter fish, crabs, shellfish and many other species. They improve water quality and slow waves, helping protect shores from erosion. And they store carbon in the seabed about 30 to 50 times faster than forests.

According to recent reports, around 70 species of seagrass can be found along the coasts of more than 150 countries. Some grow just below the surface, others at depths of 60 meters or almost 200 feet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that "Some countries have far more seagrass, particularly in the Indo-Pacific," mentioned Reusch. "There, it can play a major role in their carbon balance.".

But the value of seagrass goes beyond carbon storage. Its meadows in the Baltic are among the sea's most valuable habitats. They shelter wildlife, stabilize the seabed and act as natural filters by trapping particles and nutrients.

Planting individual seagrass shoots is painstaking work so people like Reinhard Helbig are trying to make it easier.

It has been revealed that through ZosteraTec, the start-up he co-founded, he helps restore marine habitats, including seagrass meadows damaged by offshore activity, such as wind farm construction. His work begins on the beach.

According to recent reports, "Stormy weather helps us. Waves and currents wash seagrass out of the seabed. A day or two later, it washes up here, still fresh," he noted.

The collected shoots are grown and multiplied in ZosteraTec's aquaculture. Several months later, the marine saplings are laid on a plant support. A specially developed machine binds the planted strands with biodegradable thread. The resulting lengths can be laid on the seabed with less diving work.

Recent findings suggest that "We plant here on land to cut down on underwater work. That means fewer dives, and we can do the painstaking work on shore," Helbig mentioned.

Researchers at the Geomar Helmholtz Center in Kiel are also testing fresh ways to restore seagrass across larger areas, including using seeds.

Marine ecologist Esther Thomsen reaches into an aquarium tank and pulls out a flowerpot containing seagrass.

"Ten percent of the plants in our meadows produce seeds. You can clearly see the seeds sitting inside the seed pod," she stated.

"The substantial advantage of restoring meadows from seed is greater genetic diversity. And in the future, we should be able to sow seeds over much larger areas," explained Thomsen.

Reusch from Geomar said they presently "think the most promising way to grow meadows that can withstand climate change is to plant individual shoots as a foundation, then sow seeds between them to increase genetic diversity.".

Whether a planting mission is successful is revealed months or even years later.

Thomsen and her colleagues are visiting the first seagrass meadow planted in Germany's Baltic waters in 2021. The divers count shoots, check how densely they grow and record how the meadow has developed.

Industry observers note that they then compare it with the donor meadow that supplied the plants. Only that comparison reveals whether the new crop has merely survived or is beginning to function more like a natural one.

"We've just checked the seagrass meadow, and it's really dense. We counted lots of shoots per square," Thomsen said. "It's looking really good.".

Sources indicate that derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

Same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

Industry observers note that mcInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

Sources indicate that when it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window.

From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

Recent findings suggest that if he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a new deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

Is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency blueprint being discussed and worked on in tandem.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola expects a much tougher test from Manchester United following the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino.

But Iraola expects the new face in the opposition dugout to have his charges firing on all cyclinders, despite limited time implementing new tactics.

Writing in his programme notes for Sunday's game, Iraola wrote: “Liverpool versus Manchester United can only ever create a sense of anticipation, no matter when and where the game is played and no matter who is involved.

“For us it is a privilege and it is one that comes with a lot of responsibility because of what this rivalry means. The eyes of the world will be on us and we should use this as a motivation.

“We want – and will almost certainly need – to be as near to our best as we can. That is the standard of this fixture.

In a recent development, “What people think the league table tells us in this moment is not something that we can afford to be distracted by. This is a day when this kind of thing does not matter in the same way that it might otherwise. The history of the rivalry between our two clubs tells us that.

“We should expect and prepare for the best version of United because they will definitely see this fixture as an opportunity to start showing the best of themselves, particularly under latest management.

“For this reason, we have to be focused only on delivering the strongest performance that we possibly can and I can tell you that the players have been incredibly focused on this in training from the moment they returned from the international period.".

Despite enduring a tumultuous few seasons, Man Utd have continued to enjoy success against Liverpool. They beat them home and away last season and have lost just one of the last seven meetings.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.
  • The organization reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September.
  • The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

The organization reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.

The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.

It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives said the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.

"The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act swiftly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz said in a video statement.

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.

Here are some of the key Q3 figures:.

And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing aims to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.

Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.

By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

CEO Oliver Blume aims to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.

Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the blueprint, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.

CFO Antlitz said the figures showed the urgency underlying these aims, saying the tech giant needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.

Antlitz mentioned the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.

"That is not enough in the long term," he remarked.

As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.

This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

According to recent reports, arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

Sources indicate that as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Recent findings suggest that leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

Roy Keane has predicted the biggest threat to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining the Premier League title is unlikely to come from any of their traditional rivals.

The Gunners displayed unfamiliar signs of vulnerability at St James’ Park on Saturday evening where they let a half-time lead slip, before eventually battling back to earn a 2-2 draw.

The loss of two points was compounded by an injury to goalkeeper David Raya who is now nervously anticipating the results of a forthcoming MRI scan on his damaged arm.

Manchester City’s failure to win at home against Fulham meant the failure to cling onto the lead Arsenal gained through Eberechi Eze’s first-half opener represented a missed opportunity.

With Enzo Maresca’s side in the midst of a disappointing run and the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool struggling to come to terms with the demands of their new managers, Arsenal are widely expected to defend the title they won back in May.

Indeed, their nearest challengers at present are Brighton, who are thriving under the management of Fabian Hurzeler, and Keane sees no reason why the Seagulls can’t continue to mount a challenge.

‘At this moment, yes,’ Keane told Sky Sports when asked if Brighton could emerge as the only team capable of preventing Arsenal from claiming back-to-back titles.

‘That’s because of the form they’re in, they’re goal threat and defensively they’re very, very good.

‘They’ve got a top quality manager but obviously over the next couple of months the pressure and injuries and whatever (will come).

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It has been revealed that ‘They’ve got a young team and have a lack of experience. But at this moment in time they’ve got to enjoy it and keep that pressure on Arsenal.’.

Hurzeler, who masterminded a 3-0 win over the Gunners back in September, has plenty of admirers and was recently linked with the Manchester United job.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

‘His time will come,’ Keane said when it was put to him that the German would’ve represented a better appointment than Mauricio Pochettino.

Sources indicate that ‘We talk about Poch getting close a few times and sliding doors moments. He’s done a great job and Brighton and if he left now you’d be looking at him and thinking he should’ve stuck at it a bit more.

‘We talk about loyalty in football and it’s got to work both ways. So I’m glad he continuing at Brighton and hopefully they can continue having a good season.’.

Xabi Alonso has been told that Chelsea will sack him as manager unless both performances and results improve fast.

The Blues suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Leeds at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, coming two weeks after a defeat at struggling Sunderland and a very rare home loss to rivals Tottenham.

Alonso’s substitutions have often come under question, and his introduction of Malo Gusto against Leeds was met by chants from a section of supporters of “you don’t know what you’re doing”, while there is said to be a general acceptance that his methods will take a while to implement.

The defeat leaves Chelsea sitting in ninth place, 12 points off Premier League leaders Arsenal with just 11 games of the season played.

Former Chelsea player Jason Cundy described the defeat to Leeds as “disgusting”, and expects there to be a new manager in the Blues dugout if there is not an instant improvement.

Chelsea travel to strugglers Nottingham Forest next weekend before hosting relegation-threatened Crystal Palace the week after.

According to recent reports, cundy said on talkSPORT: “We are rotten. We were so bad, it was so bad… I’m in disbelief at what I’ve just witnessed.”.

According to recent reports, in a warning to Alonso, he added: “That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won’t keep his job, I’m telling you that for nothing.

“You can’t do what you did against Sunderland (1-0 loss), you can’t do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games.

  • Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.
  • The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00.

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

The former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

Sources indicate that guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

The visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

In a recent development, "I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them.".

Almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

During their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us.".

Recent findings suggest that guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, Fresh York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

His journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

Sources indicate that the visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been announced, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

Nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would currently secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

For Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER and JACK GAUGHAN.

Published: 12:41 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 20 November 2026.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved in any wrongdoing at his former club Manchester City – but refused to rule out taking action against them if their appeal fails.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, broadcast on Friday, Berrada tackled a range of topics concerning United but his links to City, from whom he joined United in 2024, were also brought up. He worked at the club during some of the period that City were found to have broken Premier League rules.

Back in September, an independent regulatory commission found City guilty of a multitude of charges brought against them by the Premier League, with financial offences ranging between 2009 and 2018.

The scathing verdict determined that City had 'artificially inflated' their revenues and reduced costs through 'disguised funding' schemes such as 'sham' contracts.

Berrada joined City in 2011 before going on to become their chief operating officer in 2016, raising questions over whether he could end up implicated if City – who vehemently contest the charges – fail in their appeal.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted. 'I want to be very clear about this, right. I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings; there are no allegations against me, and in that sense there will be no surprises.'.

Asked if United would push for compensation should City's guilty verdict be upheld on appeal, Berrada remained tight-lipped.

Omar Berrada joined Manchester City in 2011... and moved across the city 13 years later.

Berrada has become one of the main sources of anger among United fans who have campaigned against the owners and the board.

'I don't want to comment on that because right now it's an ongoing process,' he added. 'When it runs its course we'll take our view of where is our position as Manchester United.'.

Berrada was not used as a witness in the original investigation and there are no allegations directed specifically to the now-United CEO.

City boss Enzo Maresca, meanwhile, insisted that the guilty verdicts handed down to Manchester City for financial chicanery have not affected his players despite three consecutive Premier League defeats.

City fell six points behind defending champions Arsenal in the weeks before this month’s international break amid a slew of individual high-profile errors that led to claims of Maresca’s squad being preoccupied by the uncertainty surrounding the club.

Sources indicate that the Premier League have a range of available sanctions to them were City to lose an appeal set for next month. Those would likely result in relegation to the Championship.

But Maresca does not equate that looming doomsday backdrop with a worrying run of form before they face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday lunchtime.

‘I don't think the players are thinking too much about that,’ Maresca stated. ‘If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, look at [Aston] Villa away. We had so many chances, for instance Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, or Brighton where the keeper was man of the match.

Enzo Maresca insists his stars are not thinking about the impact of the guilty verdict.

Erling Haaland claims he is 'incredibly' happy to be a City player and tops the Premier League scoring charts with nine so far this campaign.

‘Then [Nottingham] Forest when Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score for 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise. I don't think they are worried about that.’.

Haaland claimed to be ‘incredibly happy’ about being a City player in a defiant interview with Norwegian television earlier in the week, although few others have addressed the problems publicly.

Marc Guehi has previously mentioned the players are ‘relaxed’, while Phil Foden refused to discuss it when asked.

Maresca has spent the past fortnight analysing City’s ten league matches and has admitted that the team requires more balance after conceding too many goals to turnovers or counter attacks.

‘I was not thinking that we were doing everything well when we were winning games and I'm not thinking that we did everything wrong when we lost games,’ the Italian added.

‘For me it is the beginning of something long. I think we are attacking well because we are creating chances and overall we are controlling games.

In a recent development, ‘There are moments we are not controlling and we have to realise the reasons why and do better. We are conceding goals and most are avoidable from my point of view.’.

There have been occasions – like the first goal at Forest – when City’s building from the back has put them in serious trouble. Josko Gvardiol lost the ball at the City Ground after no midfielder had shown for possession.

Maresca said: ‘We reviewed things during the break. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way and try to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened for the first goal against Forest.

‘When you are building and you lose the ball in the build-up it's difficult to build with that.’.

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

In a recent development, ‘That is just a basic ball over the top of him. It’s his problem to start with.’.

Though De Ligt was the main focus of Neville’s criticism, Yoro did not escape without receiving some barbs of his own.

‘Leny Yoro can be further across but if you look at De Ligt in this channel, he’s miles away from him,’ Neville added.

In a recent development, ‘Yoro should be across, yes, he can get further around. He has to cover and he doesn’t. He reacts late, his anticipation is really poor.

‘And because he doesn’t play the ball, Yoro, it could be outside the box but it is a red card.

‘It’s so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these kinds of mistakes.’.

According to Neville, Yoro had displayed great ‘naivety’ in getting himself sent off so early in the Premier League contest.

‘He’s not happy with it, Mauricio Pochettino,’ the ex-England international continued.

‘You could argue with it, Isak just delays slightly to make sure that Yoro runs into the back of him.

‘But unfortunately, when you’re a young defender, you’re going to get caught like that and it’s naivety.’.

Switching his focus back to De Ligt, Neville said the Netherlands international had likely been ‘exposed’ as a result of playing so little football over the last 12 months.

In a recent development, ‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough,’ he went on.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.

In a recent development, ‘I have to say, Yoro’s positioning covering is really poor. It’s poor.

Industry observers note that ‘Yoro has got to be across and around the other centre-back. You’ve got to cover your mate and he doesn’t. It’s really just bad all round from Manchester United.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’.

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘It’s as bad as it gets from two centre-backs,’ the former Liverpool and England defender noted.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

Breaking: Mauricio Pochettino slams ‘unfair’ decision after Liverpool thrash Manchester United

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.
  • Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.
  • The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens quickly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

According to recent reports, ‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino said in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

In a recent development, ‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

‘We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’.

Pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

It has been revealed that ‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most crucial. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

‘That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card.’.

Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 99 min read (19742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~99 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that the genus Hordeum comprises approximately 33 species and is widely distributed across the temperate regions of Eurasia and the Americas1,2,3.
  • To maximize phylogenetic representation across the genus, we selected 27 accessions representing 24 Hordeum species, encompassing all recognized diploid genome groups1 together with representative tetraploid and hexaploid lineages (Extended Data Fig.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally key group of grasses1,2. Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. Comparative analyses reveal extensive structural variation, including inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that disrupt proximal collinearity and reflect lineage-specific genome remodelling. Single-copy gene phylogenies identify ancient hybridization, segmental exchange and introgression, revealing pervasive reticulate evolution during Hordeum diversification. We uncover widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum, with many transferred genes showing evidence of transcription and functional integration. Retrotransposon proliferation explains genome size variation and provides insights into polyploid genome evolution. Whole-genome alignments reveal contrasting evolutionary dynamics: whereas coding sequences remain highly conserved, regulatory elements undergo rapid turnover, providing a rich source of regulatory diversity for phenotypic evolution. Case studies of vernalization and glume development demonstrate how natural variation in regulatory and coding sequences contributes to flowering time and floral morphology. This comprehensive pangenomic framework establishes Hordeum as a model for studying genome evolution, structural variation and the genetic basis of adaptive traits, offering fresh avenues for barley improvement.

Sources indicate that the genus Hordeum comprises approximately 33 species and is widely distributed across the temperate regions of Eurasia and the Americas1,2,3. Hordeum is classified into two subgenera based on cytogenetic evidence: one containing the H and Xu genomes and the other containing the I and Xa genomes4. The basic chromosome number is seven, and, although most species are diploid, tetraploid and hexaploid taxa have also been described. Cultivated barley (Hordeum vulgare) is the best known and most extensively studied species, as it represents one of the earliest domesticated cereal crops. Today, barley is the world’s fourth most important grain, valued for its use in food, animal feed and brewing5. Cultivated barley and its wild progenitor (H. vulgare subsp. spontaneum) constitute a single inter-fertile gene pool, allowing for frequent gene flow between wild and cultivated forms6. This primary gene pool has long been exploited by breeders to introduce desirable traits6. Hordeum bulbosum has contributed valuable disease resistance genes through introgression7,8,9,10 due to its ability to hybridize directly with cultivated barley. The other Hordeum species are not domesticated but have important ecological and agricultural roles in ecosystem stability, environmental adaptation and forage use11,12,13,14,15. Together, Hordeum is both an agronomically important genus and a powerful model for studying crop evolution, environmental adaptation and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Factors such as incomplete lineage sorting, recurrent hybridization and gene flow partly obscure species boundaries, leaving major evolutionary questions unresolved1,2,4,16,17. Recent barley pangenomes have substantially advanced our understanding of genomic variation within cultivated barley and its closest relatives10,18,19. However, these studies were largely confined to two species (H. vulgare and H. bulbosum) and therefore could not resolve genome-wide evolutionary processes operating across the genus, including the origin of large-scale structural variation, ancient hybridization, polyploid genome evolution and the diversification of regulatory loci. Extending comparative genomic analyses to encompass the entire genus is therefore essential to capture the full breadth of diversity within the Hordeum gene pool and to facilitate both evolutionary studies and the effective utilization of wild germplasm for barley improvement. Pangenomics now offers comprehensive resources to address such complexity. In crops such as tomato, potato, maize, grapevine, citrus and cotton, genus-level pangenomes have uncovered extensive structural variations, gene presence–absence and evolutionary dynamics20,21,22,23,24. Investigating structural variations helps to explain evolutionary processes and can inform crop breeding strategies25. However, the full extent of structural variation within Hordeum remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we generated chromosome-scale genome assemblies representing all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. This comparative genomic framework provides a view of structural and regulatory genome evolution across the genus, yielding new insights into genome evolution and establishing a foundation for the utilization of wild diversity in barley improvement.

To maximize phylogenetic representation across the genus, we selected 27 accessions representing 24 Hordeum species, encompassing all recognized diploid genome groups1 together with representative tetraploid and hexaploid lineages (Extended Data Fig. 1a, Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary Figs. 1–25). The dataset comprises 22 diploid accessions, 4 tetraploid accessions and 1 hexaploid accession. Twenty-four genome sequences were assembled using PacBio HiFi accurate long reads and Hi-C data (Supplementary Tables 2 and 3 and Supplementary Figs. 26–28), using the TRITEX pipeline26,27. The sequence assemblies of H. vulgare and H. bulbosum were sourced from our previous work10,28. The previously published chromosome-level assembly of Hordeum marinum H559 (ref. 29) was updated using the TRITEX pipeline, and previously published transcriptome data, Bionano optical maps and Hi-C data of Hordeum erectifolium NGB6816 were used30. The average contig N50 of the assemblies is 39.24 Mb. Assembly sizes range from 2.90 Gb to 4.48 Gb (mean, 3.92 Gb) in diploid species and from 7.49 Gb to 8.56 Gb (mean, 8.16 Gb) in tetraploid species, whereas the single hexaploid genome has an assembly size of 10.90 Gb. Chloroplast genome assemblies range from 136,335 bp to 137,079 bp (mean, 136,840 bp) (Supplementary Table 1). High assembly quality is supported by an average long terminal repeat (LTR) assembly index (LAI) of 14.79, a consensus quality value (QV) of 67.30 and k-mer completeness of 97.22% (Supplementary Table 4). For the heterozygous diploid species H. bulbosum, the two phased haplotypes were designated as Hap1 and Hap2. For polyploid species, independently assembled chromosome sets derived from different ancestral genomes were defined as subgenomes and denoted as Sub1, Sub2 and Sub3 according to their phylogenetic relationships with diploid progenitor lineages (Fig. 1a). To assess the gene content in the Hordeum pangenome, we annotated all genomes using transcriptome data (Methods and Supplementary Tables 5 and 6). A gene consolidation method was applied to ensure high comparability of gene predictions, including those for Hordeum parodii (6x) and Hordeum gussoneanum (4x). The number of high-confidence gene models identified ranges from 35,573 for diploid Hordeum murinum to 94,943 for hexaploid H. parodii (Supplementary Table 7). We assessed the quality of the Hordeum gene annotations using BUSCO (v5.8.0) with the poales_odb12 dataset, comprising 6,282 near-universal single-copy orthologues from Poales. On average, 97.35% of BUSCO genes were identified as complete, 0.69% as fragmented and 1.84% as missing (Supplementary Table 7). Independent benchmarking with OMArk and PSAURON further confirmed the high completeness and overall quality of the gene annotations (Supplementary Table 7). Transposable element (TE) annotation using the panEDTA pipeline31 revealed that transposons constituted on average 86.12% of the genome, ranging from 83.27% to 90.35% (Supplementary Table 8).

Divergence times were inferred using 4DTV sites from genome-wide single-copy genes after excluding genomic regions with strong phylogenetic discordance (nRF > 0.21) identified in Extended Data Fig. 6c.
