To be more specific, we identified the top five positively correlated genes with summarized DEFA5 and DEFA6 scaled expression profiles across epithelium among the 3,000 HVGs as feature genes of Paneth cells. We summed up the scaled expression levels of the selected top five Paneth-associated genes for each cell as the Paneth cell feature score, and defined cells with scores exceeding 97.5th percentile of all positive scores as Paneth cells. We applied a similar procedure to identify tuft cells, with 10 tuft cell feature genes and using 95 percentile as the selection cut-off.

To establish a tissue reference for colonocyte subtype annotation in the Salmonella dataset, we subsetted to non-small intestine transit-amplifying cells, stem cells and colonocytes, integrated the data with CSS and performed subclustering based on the CSS embeddings at resolution = 0.4. We identified cluster markers using the wilcoxauc function in the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1. We selected the top 100 markers ranked by logFC from each cluster and unified them as features for comparison between in vitro and tissue colonic stem cells and colonocytes.

To further reconstruct the differentiation trajectory from stem cells to colonocytes in primary tissues (excluding transit-amplifying cells), we computed a diffusion map using the DiffusionMap function in the destiny package on the CSS space and we defined the rank of the first diffusion component (DC1) as the inferred differentiation pseudotime. We ordered the cells along the pseudotime, partitioned them into 25 bins and calculated the average gene expression of each bin. We calculated the Pearson correlation coefficients between the bin average expression levels and the bin order for each gene. The 50 genes with the strongest positive correlations were selected as pseudotime-positive correlating genes, which show higher expression levels in mature colonocytes, and the 50 genes with the strongest negative correlations as pseudotime-negative correlating genes, which show higher expression levels in stem cells and early colonocytes. We then applied these tissue-derived differentiation-related genes on the sorted infection dataset. We used the AddModuleScore function in Seurat based on normalized RNA expression values of the pseudotime positively and negatively correlating genes separately. A composite differentiation score of the cells in the chip was defined as the difference between the positive and negative module scores. We ordered the colonocytes according to the differentiation score from premature to mature, partitioned them into 25 bins and calculated the average gene expression of each bin. The obtained bin average gene expression profiles are defined as expression profiles along the reconstructed pre-mature-to-mature colonocyte differentiation trajectory.

To create a unified peak list across samples, we called open chromatin-accessible regions in each sample using MACS2 (v2.2.9.1) with the CallPeaks function and then quantified them with FeatureMatrix in Signac. We only kept regions located on standard chromosomes. We annotated peaks to most nearby genes using the annotatePeak function in ChIPseeker based on the Ensemble (v98) annotation. We only retained cells with ATAC UMI count between 200 and 50,000, RNA UMI count less than 20,000, RNA gene number between 500 and 5,000, mitochondrial percentage less than 50%, nucleosome signal (calculated by NucleosomeSignal) less than 1, transcription start site enrichment score (calculated by TSSEnrichment) less than 1 and hg38 genome blacklist ratio less than 0.5%. We ran the same pipeline of scRNA-seq data from read count normalization to dimension reduction and clustering as described in the previous section (‘Preprocessing and cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq data’). For the scATAC-seq data, we performed term frequency-inverse document frequency normalization on read counts using the RunTFIDF function. We defined the regions with over 1% detection rate as top features and RunSVD based on the top features. We projected cells into two-dimension UMAP embeddings and FindNeighbors based on top 2–50 latent semantic indexing.

In a recent development, we performed major epithelial cell-type annotation on RNA cluster level based on canonical cell-type marker expression. We subsetted to colonic stem cell and colonocyte clusters, calculated the Spearman correlation coefficients between in vitro and tissue stem cell to colonocyte clusters using the in vitro-expressed colonic stem cell and colonocyte feature genes defined in the tissue reference. We performed hierarchical clustering on the in vitro clusters based on the similarity profiles and classified them into stem cells and four colonocyte subtypes indicating differential maturity accordingly. Colonocyte clusters with mostly exclusive presence in the Salmonella-infected sample were defined as infection-specific colonocyte clusters. We transferred RNA-level cell-type annotations to ATAC data, and merged subtypes that could not be clearly resolved by ATAC data as annotations on the ATAC level.

Sources indicate that we performed differential analysis for co-clustered S.Tm infection and control cells in each cluster of stem cells, colonocytes and goblet cells, which have sufficient cell numbers for robust estimation. For infection-specific clusters, which have less than 20 control cells in the clusters, we first identified matched control sample cells for each infected sample cell using get.knnx of the FNN package with k = 1 in the top 20 principal component space. We identified DEGs between matched control and infected cells using the wilcoxauc function by the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1. We applied the same procedure to identify DEGs in the epithelium induced by TRM cell co-culture except that we did not need to use the k-nearest neighbour search approach to get matched control cells as there was no condition-specific cluster.

To identify DARs between Salmonella-infected and control conditions, we implemented a statistical framework based on linear regression modelling of binarized chromatin accessibility data, with sequencing depth (UMI counts) as covariate. Specifically, for each open chromatin region i, we fitted:.

Null model: glm(e ~ UMIcounts, family = binomial).

Full model: glm(e ~ UMIcounts + condition, family = binomial).

where e represents the binarized accessibility state vector for region i across all cells. We applied a Chi-squared test comparing the two models using ANOVA. Regions were considered differentially accessible if they had Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05 and showed at least a 0.5% difference in the proportion of cells with the region accessible between Salmonella-infected and control conditions.

It has been revealed that we reconstructed the gene regulatory networks from the scMultiome data along the stem-cell-to-coloncyte trajectory and each of the stem cell, colonocyte and goblet cell types shared by both control and infection conditions using Pando83 separately. We used the infection-induced DEGs and 5,000 HVGs of each data as input HVGs for Pando. We constrained our candidate regulatory regions to be either conserved in mammals (defined in phastConsElements20Mammals.UCSC.hg38 provided by Pando) or overlapped with ENCODE regions (defined in SCREEN.ccRE.UCSC.hg38 provided by Pando), and showing significantly correlated profiles with HVGs as output by LinkPeaks in Signac at the default distance threshold of 500 kb. We ran find_motifs and used the Pando-provided transcription factor-binding site (TFBS) motif database compiled from JASPAR and CIS-BP as reference for Pando to identify TFBS in candidate regulatory regions. We ran the infer_grn function with a Gaussian generalized linear model (model = ‘glm’) to infer regulatory coefficients from log-normalized transcript counts and binarized peak counts summarized to SLM algorithm-defined ATAC clusters (resolution = 10). We identified transcription factor–target gene modules using the find_modules function with default settings. We combined the modules from different datasets as inferred transcription factor–target pairs.

For visualization, we selected the condition-dependent DEGs with the top 500 absolute value of expression log-transformed fold change between conditions and the union set of the top three-correlated Pando-predicted transcription factors of each selected DEGs. We calculated pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients of expression profiles across cell types and conditions between selected genes, reduced the dimension of obtained correlation matrix to 20 principal components using prcomp_irlba in the irlba package and further projected genes to two-dimension embeddings using umap in the uwot package with the obtained principal components as input.

We ran the AddMotifs function in Signac to add the TFBS motifs information on our detected open chromatin regions and obtained a motif occurrence matrix. To identify TFBS motifs over-represented in open chromatin regions with increased accessibility upon infection in each cell type, we ran FindMotifs in Signac on the top 200 upregulated accessible regions, with 30,000 open chromatin regions with matched overall GC content retrieved by the MatchRegionStats function as background.

We defined three comparisons to characterize the luminal effects: (1) ΔSPI-1/2 non-invaded (ΔSPI-1/2Out, GFP−) versus non-infected, (2) WT non-invaded (WTOut, GFP−) versus non-infected, and (3) WTOut versus ΔSPI-1/2Out; and three for intracellular effects: (1) WT invaded (WTIn, GFP+) versus WTOut, (2) ΔsteE invaded (ΔsteEIn, GFP+) versus WTIn, and (3) ΔSPI-2In versus WTIn. We subsetted to colonocytes. Genes detected in at least 50 colonocytes were retained, excluding features with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ‘ENSG’. Pairwise comparisons were conducted between predefined experimental conditions within each colonocyte cluster. Comparisons were performed only when at least 20 cells were available in at least one condition. When one of the conditions contained fewer than 20 cells, we supplemented with cells from other clusters of the same condition that were defined as nearest neighbours of the other condition, using get.knnx of the FNN package with k = 1 based on Euclidean distance in the top 20 principal component space. Differential expression testing was performed using the wilcoxauc function of the presto R package on normalized RNA expression values. We identified DEGs between conditions per cluster using the wilcoxauc function by the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1.

We then pooled genes defined as significant DEGs in at least one comparison in at least one cluster as the union set of condition DEGs. We then calculated the colonocyte average expression levels of each condition. We calculated the expression difference between WTOut and non-infected—namely, diff_WT_vs_NI, where positive values indicate upregulation in WTOut versus non-infected—and between WTIn and WTOut—namely, diff_WT_GFP_vs_WT, where positive values indicate upregulation in WTIn versus WTOut. We ranked the gene according to diff_WT_vs_NI, took the top 50 genes as feature genes and used the AddModuleScore function to calculate the luminal effect gene module score, and applied the same procedure for diff_WT_GFP_vs_WT values for intracellular effect gene module score.

According to recent reports, we used CellChat (v2)84 to infer intracellular communications between co-cultured intestinal epithelial cells and TRM cells. Normalized expression data were extracted from the epithelium and TRM cell combined Seurat RNA assay, and cell-type labels were used to group cells for interaction analysis. We used the built-in human CellChatDB database as reference for ligand–receptor interactions. To reduce computational cost, we subsetted the expression data to include only signalling genes present in the database. Overexpressed genes and interactions were identified using the identifyOverExpressedGenes and identifyOverExpressedInteractions functions. Communication probabilities were computed using the computeCommunProb function with type = truncatedMean and trim = 0.05. We subsetted to interactions between proximal small intestinal enterocytes and immune cell types, excluding proliferating CD4+ T cells for visualization.

In a recent development, read alignment, gene expression quantification and cell filtering of the VASA-seq data were performed by Single Cell Discoveries. In brief, raw sequencing data were processed using Cutadapt (v4.9) to remove adapter sequences and homopolymers, followed by Ribodetector (v0.3.1) to filter out ribosomal reads. Processed reads were then aligned to the reference genome using STARsolo (v2.7.11b), with the parameter–soloFeatures set to GeneFull_Ex50pAS. The human reference genome used was GRCh38, ENSEMBL release 103. The S.Tm reference genome was downloaded from EnsemblBacteria Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. 14028S str. LT2 14028S (GCA_000022165) release 62. The resulting single-cell-level gene count matrices were used as inputs for downstream analysis in R.

To improve the gene annotation for the S.Tm genome, we performed sequence alignment for the genes in the S.Tm strain 14028S annotation against the S.Tm strain 14028 annotation (GCF_028596185.1_ASM2859618v1). Out of the 1,542 genes with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ENSB, 242 were mapped to annotated genes with common names in the S.Tm 14028 annotation by blastn85,86 with more than 90% of sequence similarity.

Recent findings suggest that cells without GFP signal, UMI count of less than 3,500 or External RNA Controls Consortium (ERCC) counts of less than 450 were excluded. Raw counts were normalized using the NormalizeData function in Seurat with a scale factor of 10,000.

According to FACS index sorting values, cells with GFP < 500 were defined as GFP−, 500 or more and less than 2,000 as GFPlo, 2,000 or more and 10,000 or less as GFPint, and more than 10,000 as GFPhi. For human genes, only genes detected in at least 10% of cells in at least one GFP signal group were included in the differentially expressed test. For each retained gene, expression was modelled using two nested linear models. The reduced model included log-transformed total UMI counts per cell and the percentage of mitochondrial reads as technical covariates, whereas the full model additionally included the GFP signal group as a factor. The contribution of the GFP signal group was assessed by ANOVA comparing the full and reduced models. Genes with Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05 were considered differentially expressed. To assign directionality, we calculated the difference in average expression between the GFPhi and GFPlo groups and assigned the directionality accordingly.

For S.Tm, we applied the same differentially expressed test strategy, but only included GFP+ cells for comparison. Given the sparsity of the bacteria transcripts, we reduced the detection rate cut-off to 1%. After further excluding ERCC transcripts and features with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ENSB, 3,137 genes were left as input for the differentially expressed test. We used nominal P < 0.05 as the cut-off to get marginally significant bacterial DEG.

Further information on research design is available in the Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary linked to this article.

The ArrayExpress accession number for the fastq files of non-sorted scRNA-seq and scMultiome data reported in this paper is E-MTAB-16821. The raw and processed sorted infection scRNA-seq and VASA-seq data could be accessed via E-MTAB-17487 and E-MTAB-17486. Additional supporting materials, including processed single-cell data with cell-type annotation, statistically significant differentially accessible chromatin regions upon S.Tm infection and transcription factor–target regulomes inferred by Pando based on the S.Tm infection dataset are available at Mendeley Data (https://doi.org/10.17632/3jpvw4t4gr). Fragment files of scMultiome are available at Mendeley Data (https://doi.org/10.17632/8pt6w6fc7m). The raw mass spectrometry proteomic files and corresponding metadata tables and scripts used are available in the MassIVE repository (UCSD) under the accession code MSV000102372. The raw flow cytometry data files used to generate the immune UMAP have been deposited in the Zenodo repository87 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21786694). Source data underlying all graphical representations used in the figures are provided as Supplementary Information. Public adult intestine multi-region scRNA-seq datasets were retrieved from an interactive website of the Space-Time Gut Cell Atlas (https://www.gutcellatlas.org/)79, ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-10187)81 and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE185224)80.

The core scripts of single-cell data analysis are available on GitHub (https://github.com/devsystemslab/Host-microbe_interaction_model/).

R.L.-S., M.F.H., Q.Y., M.N., N.G. and J.G.C. conceived the study. R.L.-S., M.F.H., Q.Y., N.G. and J.G.C. wrote the manuscript. M.N. designed and fabricated the fluidic device and crypt stamps, with support from J.A. and S.M. M.P.L. contributed to the development of the fluidic device holding the tissues. M.N. and R.L.-S. generated the artwork design. M.F.H. and R.L.-S. designed and performed most of the experiments in the article. R.L.-S., M.F.H., M.N., N.A. and J.B. optimized the epithelium growth conditions. M.F.H. isolated the organoid lines and TRM cells from primary tissue. R.L.-S., M.F.H., M.A.-B., L.G.-T. and S.S. performed scRNA-seq, scMultiome and VASA-seq experiments. M.A.-B. and L.G.-T. generated the sequencing libraries. Q.Y. performed the computational analysis of scRNA-seq and scMultiome data, with support and data interpretation from R.L.-S., S.S. and M.F.H. M.F.H., R.L.-S. and J.A. co-developed the histomold. I.C. and S.T. performed the FFPE processing, sectioning, H&E and AlcianBlue–PAS stainings, with support from M.F.H. M.F.H. performed the immunohistochemistry and mIF stainings, imaging and analysis with support from R.L.-S. and M.N. M.F.H., R.L.-S., M.N. and L.K. performed whole-mount stainings and imaging. M.F.H., K.K. and S.K. performed the flow cytometry experiments and analysis of immune cells. R.L.-S., D.C. and I.C.-A. performed the flow cytometry and image stream experiments and analysis of epithelial cells. L.K., A.M.F. and M.F.H. performed the cytokine measurements. N.A., S.R.V., Y.B. and J.B. generated the organoid reporter lines. J.F., A.A. and C.S. performed and processed the proteomic measurements. Live imaging was performed by M.F.H., R.L.-S. and M.N., and analysed by M.B. M.H. and D.B. generated and provided the S.Tm strains. T.R. and F.G. supported with data interpretation. a) Picture of a chip-slide with culture medium, including a 3D-rendered image of the cross-section of the chip-slide containing three individual chip segments and an image of the micropatterned stamp with a representative bright-field image of an engineered intestine cross-section, e > 15. b) Time course of biomimetic epithelium formation from the stamped empty ECM to epithelium coverage and maturation. Scale bars: 500 µm. c) Quantification of viable crypts of 16 donors from duodenum, ileum and colon, d = 16. d) Representative EDF brightfield image of a Z-stack, showing the top-view of a day-9 epithelium, e = 3. Scale bar: 200 µm. The magnified insert (top) shows a 3D-reconstruction of the epithelium with crypts penetrating into the matrix. The magnified insert (bottom) shows an EDF image of a Z-stack in the crypt area. Scale bar: 50 µm. e) Representative EDF fluorescent image of selected Z-stacks with magnified insert, showing an iCas9 CDH1-mScarlet3 day-9 duodenal epithelium with tight E-Cadherin+ adherens junctions (red), e = 6. Scale bar: 100 µm. f) Overview of the high-throughput histo-processing workflow using 3D-printed histomold facilitating co-planar embedding of up to fifty engineered epithelia at once. Consecutive sections subjected to H&E and mIF to evaluate the spatial organization and maturation of a duodenal epithelium at day 6. Scale bars: 100 µm.

It has been revealed that a-c) Representative mIF cross-section of engineered duodenal, ileal and colonic epithelia in direct comparison to the donor-matched primary tissue (ileum not matched), highlighting the stem-niche specific SOX9+ (cyan) and transit-amplifying Ki67+ cells (pink), matching abundance of MUC2+ goblet cells (green) and high expression of the region-enriched absorptive lineage marker (orange) in the E-Cadherin+ epithelium (grey). The duodenal epithelium was marked by strong expression APOA4+ enterocytes, matching the parental tissue. Expression of distal FABP6+ enterocytes in the top-layer of the engineered epithelium matched ileal tissue. The colonic epithelium exhibited CA1+ colonocytes at comparable levels to the organ of origin, e = 4. Scale bars: 50 µm.

a) Schematic of the multiplexed scRNA-seq characterization of day-10 engineered intestinal epithelia from duodenum, ileum and colon. b) Recovered cells from each of the sequenced donors, highlighting the equal contribution of each donor to the resulting atlas. c) Stacked barplot showing reproducible cell-type percentages of each of the individual donors. d) Heatmap showing a selected set of enriched biological processes (BP) and molecular functions (MF) derived from the top 500 marker genes (Wilcoxon test, logFC > log(1.1), padj <0.05) of enterocytes (duodenum, ileum) and colonocytes (colon). The enrichment score for each term is calculated by subtracting the significant -log10 transformed hypergeometric test BH-corrected P value of the region of interest and the average of those from the other two regions. e) Heatmap showing expression patterns of adult duodenum tissue zonation markers along stem cell to enterocyte diffusion map inferred trajectory of the engineered epithelium. f) Complementary to Fig. 1l. IHC stainings of SLC5A1, SLC10A2, and SLC26A2 in one cross-section containing duodenal, ileal and colonic epithelia, e = 1. Scale bar: 100 µm. g) Comparison of enteroendocrine cell (EEC) and goblet cell proportions, derived from the day-10 scRNA-seq dataset and coloured by the region of origin. Bars represent the mean ± SD. dDuo = 2 and d=4Col (dots), n = 3 pooled per donor prior sequencing. h) Whole mount staining image showing goblet cells (green) and EECs (red) in one engineered epithelium. EDF fluorescent image of a Z-stack. Scale bar: 100 µm. i-j) (i) Dot plot showing the average expression of the main intestinal EEC-derived hormones at day 10. The expression is shown for the subclustered EEC subpopulations, identified as different subtypes. (j) Stacked barplot showing the proportions of the subclustered EEC populations within their region of origin.

According to recent reports, a) mIF staining of a cross-section of colonic epithelium with accumulated mucus (4 days, 5 μl) and 24 h of S.Tm co-culture, showing S.Tm (yellow) in the luminal side, areas with epithelium breach, and intracellular invasion. STAT3 activation (p-STAT3; cyan) appears in invaded cells, colocalizing with intracellular bacteria (magnified inserts; white arrows), e = 5. Heatmap showing the scaled KEGG pathway enrichment of each gene module which is defined as the min-max normalized -log10-transformed hypergeometric test nominal P-value (right). e) Z-score scaled expression of infection-specific colonocyte subtype 2-enriched genes across colonocyte subtypes. f) Dot plot showing distinct transcription program of infection-specific colonocyte subtype 2. g) TF expression logFC between infection-specific colonocyte subtype 2 and matched control cells. *** indicates significant enrichment of TF binding motifs in open chromatin regions with increased accessibility in infection-specific colonocyte subtype 2 as compared to matched control cells, BH-corrected hypergeometric test Pvalue < 2.2e-06. h) Normalized expression levels of S.Tm infection upregulated genes and the chromatin accessibility levels of their regulatory regions across epithelial cell types in different conditions, highlighting features associated with infection-specific colonocyte subtype 2 (BACH1, SBNO2, IGFBP1, AHRR, CASP5), ubiquitous (CCL20, DUOXA2) and infection-specific colonocyte subtype 1 (VEGFA).

Latest Update: Allegri’s half-time advice to Napoli: ‘Try smiling, and we might get a goal’

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Soccernews

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.
  • Massimiliano Allegri asked for his Napoli team to play with some happiness and freedom in their Serie A clash with Torino.
  • Scott McTominay netted the decisive goal at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where Napoli won 1-0.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Massimiliano Allegri asked for his Napoli team to play with some happiness and freedom in their Serie A clash with Torino.

Scott McTominay netted the decisive goal at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where Napoli won 1-0.

It marked Napoli's first league win in three games, since they beat Monza on October 28.

Napoli had 13 shots in the first half, worth a combined 1.34 expected goals, but they could not find the breakthrough.

And Allegri explained what he asked of his players during his half-time team talk.

He told Sky Sport Italia: "The mood wasn’t right because we had so many chances, I told them at half-time to try smiling and we might get a goal.

"They did really well to win this game, while suffering against a strong opponent. Perhaps it is positive that we won under pressure, but we also should’ve done better controlling the tempo, moving the ball from one side to the other.

"The lads did very well in defending on set plays and corner kicks.".

McTominay is the only central midfielder to have scored at least 25 goals across the last three seasons in the top five European leagues (since the start of 2024-25).

He has scored four goals against Torino in Serie A, and proved the difference here.

Full time #NapoliTorino 1-0 #ForzaNapoliSempre https://t.co/97wT7xGng4.

— Official SSC Napoli (@en_sscnapoli) November 21, 2026.

When Antonio Vergara went off injured in the first half, Allegri brought on Kevin De Bruyne and played the former Manchester City playmaker deeper, allowing McTominay to push on.

"The fun thing about this job is finding solutions. I am starting to get to know these players, I thought De Bruyne could do better as a support for the striker, but in this situation, McTominay was more useful," Allegri added.

"I just told McTominay not to be already in the position right behind [Rasmus] Hojlund, but to run into that space, as it would make him harder to mark.

"If he is already there and not mobile, then obviously he's going to be easier to control, but he started to move between the lines and did better.".

Allegri has become the first coach in Serie A history to accumulate 1,100 points, but Napoli's focus now turns to a Champions League clash with Man City.

"We need to be realistic, because as I said when the fixture list was first drawn up, our Champions League qualification would be decided in the final three matches," Allegri said.

"On Tuesday we need a good performance, try to get a result, but also know that we’ve got to sort our Serie A position first.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 13:48.
  • Bayern Munich and England star Harry Kane has vowed to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing ankle surgery.
  • The striker sustained an ankle ligament injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw against FC Koln on Friday evening.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 13:48.

Bayern Munich and England star Harry Kane has vowed to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing ankle surgery.

The striker sustained an ankle ligament injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw against FC Koln on Friday evening.

Kane attempted to carry on after being caught in a tackle from Koln defender Joel Schmied before he received treatment and made way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute.

Bayern released a statement after the game, revealing Kane would be out for a "few months" with a "torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle".

Industry observers note that in a fresh enhancement on Saturday morning, Bayern noted: "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight following the syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle, which he sustained in yesterday’s Bundesliga match against 1. FC Köln.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program.".

Kane also shared a defiant message on social media, accompanied by an image of him sitting on a hospital bed with his left foot in a protective boot.

In a recent development, "The highs and lows of life!" Kane wrote. "Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

“‘Tough times don’t last, tough people do’ - my guy Julian Edelman (three-time Super Bowl winner) told me this one!

According to recent reports, “Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!”.

According to recent reports, the highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season! “Tough times don’t last, tough people do” - my guy @Edelman11 told me this one! Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut! ❤️?

With Kane likely to be out until the end of February, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany will have to come up with solutions to negate the impact of being without his star striker.

Ismael Saibari can play as a centre-forward, but he is at the moment sidelined with the same injury as Kane, putting him out of action until the start of February.

Serge Gnabry is also on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back until the turn of the year, leaving Kompany without another potential candidate to fill the void created by Kane's absence.

Noah Codjo-Evora is an option if Kompany decides to put his faith in youth, but the 19-year-old is unlikely to start regularly given the fact he only made his first-team debut as a substitute on Friday.

That means Kompany will likely opt to field a false nine in the coming weeks and months, which is a role Lennart Karl played when Kane went off against Koln.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.

Sources indicate that in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Bartesaghi was the first to properly get in, cementing his spot in the starting eleven last season, while Cisse has been the massive breakthrough this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

Cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

Sources indicate that “He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”.

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward….

“Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

“They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a newly introduced role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”.

In a recent development, camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

According to recent reports, “I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

Sources indicate that “A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”.

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

Sources indicate that “I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

“It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”.

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

Industry observers note that “For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”.

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

In a recent development, “Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he shows it every time he comes to us.

According to recent reports, “If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

According to recent reports, “He can play in any position on the flank. In my opinion, if he starts 50 meters from the goal, he can perform at his best.”.

Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle

📅 14 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.
  • It has been revealed that in what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes.
  • According to recent reports, city will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

It has been revealed that in what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

According to recent reports, city will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

Industry observers note that the data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

It could have been a hat-trick. It could even have been four as Haaland, taking the captain’s armband as Rúben Dias was withdrawn during the interval, clipped the top of the crossbar with a header and then was denied by goalkeeper Matvei Safonov as the striker slid in.

In a recent development, “Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis [Enrique, PSG’s coach] said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky,” Maresca claimed before being asked whether he would relish facing PSG again, later in this competition. “My feeling is we are there. We are close,” he added.

In a recent development, did City deserve a draw? No one was predicting that at half-time as they were suffering as comprehensive a defeat as was inflicted by the commission. Accused of “sham” contracts to inflate income, this was a sham of a performance, made all the more emphatic because of how brilliant PSG, and their exceptional 21-year-old winger Désiré Doué, were.

Désiré Doué with a brilliant finish from range to give PSG an early lead in Manchester 😮‍💨 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/Uwilx7I37H.

There is a certain irony that it was PSG who inflicted this defeat, ending City’s run of eight wins from eight in all competitions under Maresca.

It was a meeting of two clubs empowered more than any other by the riches of Gulf states: Abu Dhabi versus Qatar. Both have also had their run-ins over money. Both were sanctioned, but escaped full bans by Uefa for breaching financial fair play rules.

The question, also, was: would the eighth meeting of these clubs in the Champions League in the last 11 seasons be the last for some time?

In a recent development, so we should savour it and we did. That included Pep Guardiola on his first return to the Etihad – in a sign of solidarity – after quitting at the end of last season. Not that he savoured much of what he saw as PSG dominated City to such an extent that their fans adopted the “Poznan” celebration and the home supporters were silenced.

City could have gone in front before they conceded with the erratic Safonov – who was Gianluigi Donnarumma’s understudy and has become his unlikely replacement – punching a corner against his own crossbar before Antoine Semenyo shot the rebound over.

Then PSG ran all over City. They broke far too easily and scored far too easily. Not once, but twice, to go 2-0 up.

For the first, PSG countered, with City struggling to cover, and Doué caught out Donnarumma with a low shot inside his right-hand post from 22 yards.

Then PSG sliced through City’s defence with Ousmane Dembélé scooping the ball across the area to Doué who returned it back. Dembélé stooped to head home.

Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG's lead just 2 minutes after they scored the first 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/MxhJ3oCWpC.

Industry observers note that after Achraf Hakimi headed against the inside of a post and City could not clear, the ball came back with Warren Zaïre-Emery flicking on Maghnes Akliouche’s cut-back. It ran to Vitinha who slammed in a first-time shot. It was the first time City had ever conceded three goals at home in the first half of this competition.

Vitinha with a BEAUTY to put PSG three up after just 30 minutes 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/vgqkI6kI3h.

In a recent development, maybe it was too easy. Maybe City could not continue to be so dominated but it was as if a switch was flicked when the teams returned. The chances came for City. Enzo Fernández should have scored from a close-range header and Haaland did, glancing in an inswinging Ndiaye cross.

Industry observers note that finally the City fans found their voices but then they were silenced. What a calamity for Donnarumma as he got a hand to Akliouche’s shot on the turn, but only palmed the ball up in the air before it bounced into the net.

But City did not stop. Nuno Mendes headed Josko Gvardiol’s flick off the line, Fernández hit a post before Bouaddi set up Haaland and he swept the ball past Safonov.

Erling Haaland gets his second of the night, and the game could be back on 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/sFZ0eT2Egz.

In a recent development, there was time for PSG to miss a penalty, with Donnarumma comfortably saving Ferran Torres’s weak effort as City bravely continued to push. They lost, but it did not quite feel like that.

Sources indicate that I think our start was quite good until the first goal. Then we conceded the second after one [more] minute and that created bad feelings so we struggled.

Second half we were much, much, much better and we probably deserved even something more.

Recent findings suggest that it was strange to be honest because until the first goal we were in the game. We created things, didn’t concede and then the first goal led to the second one. When you concede two goals in two minutes it could [get] even worse.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

Sources indicate that after Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has mentioned he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having mentioned that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 13:47, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 13:58.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has recalled goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez for Saturday's Premier League fixture against Leeds United.

Despite Martinez having proven his recovery from a fractured jaw for Argentina over the international break, many felt that Mike Penders would retain his place between the sticks.

Instead, Alonso has opted to hand Martinez a way back into the starting lineup in what is one of four changes from the 1-0 defeat at Sunderland.

Josh Acheampong has shaken off a minor fitness issue to take the spot of Marco Palestra at right-back.

Estevao Willian returns on the right flank, with Jordan Henderson dropping down to the substitutes' bench.

Meanwhile, Alonso has selected a frontline number nine, with Emanuel Emegha getting the nod over Pedro Neto for what is his first Premier League start.

Moises Caicedo has passed a fitness test to take his place in midfield.

As for Leeds, Daniel Farke has made just the one alteration to his Leeds XI for the game in West London.

Noah Okafor has been rewarded for his goal as a substitute versus Spurs with a place in the final third ahead of Lukas Nmecha.

Sean Longstaff will either line up in a three-player midfield or be used as one of two number 10s.

Chelsea XI: Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Lavia, Caicedo; Estevao, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha.

Subs: Penders, Subuloye, Gusto, Palestra, Barco, Henderson, Neto, Quenda, Welbeck.

Leeds United XI: Trafford; Bogle, Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic, Gudmundsson; Ampadu, Longstaff, Tanaka; Okafor, Calvert-Lewin.

Subs: Zetterer, Bard, Rodon, Bijol, Stach, Aaronson, James, Wilson, Nmecha.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia feels his team were by far the better team against Real Betis, labelling their last-gasp draw as a "bittersweet" result.

Kike Salas netted late on in Saturday's derby to snatch a 1-1 draw for Sevilla, who fell behind to Antony's effort early in the second half.

Sevilla had 25 shots to Betis' six, and accumulated chances worth 2.3 expected goals to their opponent's 0.6.

They registered 47 touches in the Betis box and also hit the woodwork, though Garcia's team did fail to create a substantial chance.

And Garcia said a point was the least Sevilla deserved.

"We drew at the end, and it's a tremendous joy, but we all have a bittersweet feeling, because we were much better [than Betis]," he said.

"We had 25 shots on goal compared to just six, playing in the opposition's half, creating more scoring opportunities.

"I think it's one of the matches we dominated the most.".

Hang it in the Louvre https://t.co/6XAiWr0YwU.

— Sevilla FC (@SevillaFC_ENG) November 22, 2026.

Garcia did concede, though, that Sevilla are lacking real quality up top.

"We're lacking talent up front, not from the forwards themselves, but moments of inspiration in the final third," he added.

Sources indicate that "Football is about quality; it's about the difference in talent. But the team deserves respect. We keep adding points and fighting until the end.

"I respect [Betis coach] Manuel [Pellegrini] because I'm fond of him, and coaches come to press conferences wearing their team's shirt, but if anyone deserved to win, it was Sevilla.".

Betis defender Marc Bartra, however, felt Sevilla got lucky, as he claimed Salas should have been sent off for an earlier tackle on Isco.

"It's clear we deserved to take all three points, absolutely," Bartra said.

"They equalised with a player who should have been sent off. I prefer to focus on how the team performed.

"It was clear he stepped on Isco's foot. I saw it live and on replay. The images speak for themselves. For this to happen at this stage with all the cameras, I'd rather not say what I really think.".

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.

The German hobbled off late on in Celtic's win over Kilmarnock almost a fortnight ago with a scan subsequently revealing that he sustained ligament damage.

One of the Parkhead side's star men since signing from Paderborn in the summer, Baur's absence is a major blow for O'Neill ahead of a defining period in the season.

While the manager will look to the likes of Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg to step up domestically, he will also consider using a UEFA rule to make a change to his European squad ahead of Thursday's match away to Torreense in Portugal.

The rule allows clubs to make an alteration to the squad they submitted for the group stage if the injury is expected to sideline the player for more than 60 days from when it occurred.

Van den Berg, Jota, Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka weren't on the original 25-man list so would be options to be drafted in.

German midfielder Mika Baur could miss up to 10 weeks of action after injuring his ankle.

'I would definitely check with the medical staff and Mika, for a start,' noted O'Neill.

'And speaking to him yesterday, he's really upbeat about it. Obviously, he will have that boot on for a few weeks.

'I suppose deep down, if it was, let's say, 10 weeks, that's taking you right through to the end of January. I can't see us seeing him in the next six weeks.'.

Baur's form following his £4.5million move has been good enough for him to win his first full cap for Germany after being called up by newly introduced manager Jurgen Klopp.

It has been revealed that 'He was doing great for us,' added O'Neill. 'It is a blow. And it seemed so innocuous at the time.

'I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he'd landed on. It's just gone over. It's a real shame. He was playing great for us.

'There's things that he can't do for a while.'.

O'Neill revealed that Benjamin Nygren is also an injury doubt for Saturday's match with St Mirren.

'He didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning,' he explained. 'He's got a sore heel. He missed out the second game in Sweden's run.

'He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks, so we'll see how he is tomorrow.'.

19-year-old summer signing Joel van den Berg could make his first Celtic outing this weekend.

Van den Berg hasn't played for the first team since joining from PSV Eindhoven for £3.4m in the summer with an injury impeding his progress.

But the 19-year-old could be in line for his first-team debut against the Buddies.

It has been revealed that 'I had a little chat to him,' said O'Neill. 'He trained this morning, he didn't train yesterday. We played a bounce game during the week, Tuesday against St Johnstone.

In a recent development, 'He played in that game, came off and he was definitely limping for a while. He had a couple of days' treatment.

'In the overall scheme of things, whether it's tomorrow or in the next week or two, I'd hope to see him make his mark.

'As I said to him yesterday, "When you get in, it's really up to you".'.

O'Neill anticipates a stern test from a St Mirren side who often have not picked up the positive results their performances have merited under Craig McLeish.

'The overall job he's done has been terrific, really terrific,' stated the Celtic manager.

'They're having a wee tough time at this minute, obviously, with results, but his overall contributions, I'd say it's been excellent.

'There are some really fine coaches in Scotland, genuinely, and I don't want to sound patronising or sycophantic, but there are.

'We were up against one two weeks ago against Kilmarnock [Neil McCann], so I've got a lot of time for those boys who are coming through and who, to my mind, are every bit as good of coaches as quite a number down south.'.

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayinidir is reportedly at risk of having his Celta Vigo loan stay terminated in the latest year.

Bayinidir was allowed to leave in the summer after Man United recruited Karl Darlow to be Senne Lammens' deputy.

The Turkey international joined Celta on a season-long loan move with the objective of enjoying regular game time.

However, Bayindir has experienced a similar situation to the one he had at Man United, having been forced to play a backup role to Ionut Radu.

Having been overlooked in La Liga and the Europa League, Bayindir's only appearance for Celta came in the recent 5-0 victory over Salamanca in the Copa del Rey.

With Bayindir's playing situation unlikely to change, Faro de Vigo via Sports Witness are reporting that Celta have a major decision to make over the goalkeeper's loan spell.

The Galician club are assessing the situations of their loan players who lack prominence and are not ruling out the prospect of cutting Bayindir's loan short.

From Man United's perspective, there is no indication they will look to terminate the goalkeeper's loan stint, but it could still end prematurely if Celta or the player express frustration with how the move is panning out.

Bayindir headed out to Galicia after being deemed surplus to requirements under former Man United head coach Michael Carrick.

While Mauricio Pochettino has since replaced Carrick in the Old Trafford dugout, the managerial change is unlikely to affect Bayindir's status at the club.

Even if his current loan switch is cut short, the 28-year-old will likely leave in January in another temporary deal or a permanent transfer.

In truth, it is only a matter of time until Bayindir leaves Old Trafford on a permanent basis, with his contract set to expire in the summer of 2028.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz visits the demilitarized zone between North and South Korea.

Merz draws on Germany's own reunification experience, saying division causes suffering.

Two German leaders, two parallel missions across Asia.

While President Frank-Walter Steinmeier sought to reinforce ties with China in Beijing, Chancellor Friedrich Merz toured Japan, South Korea and Singapore, promoting closer cooperation among what he calls the world's "middle powers.".

Together, the visits highlight Berlin's effort to lower risks without decoupling from China.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Germany's annual inflation rate eased to 2.8% in October from 3.3% in September, with economists pointing to the government's fuel tax cut as the main reason.

It has been revealed that preliminary figures from the Federal Statistical Office showed energy prices rose 12.2% compared with a year earlier, down from 14.9% in September. Services inflation slowed to 2.5%, while food inflation remained at 0.4%.

Recent findings suggest that "The decisive factor was the fuel tax cut," noted Silke Tober of the Macroeconomic Policy Institute. The reduction took effect in October and runs through December, although rising crude oil prices partly offset the savings at the pump.

Sources indicate that ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski said higher energy costs had yet to feed through into broader price increases. Unlike during the 2022 energy crisis, consumers were unwilling or unable to absorb substantially higher prices, he said.

But economists warned the relief could prove temporary. "Gas and oil prices have risen significantly again in recent weeks," said Stephanie Schoenwald, an economist at Germany's state-owned development bank KfW, citing continuing conflicts and lower inventories.

German President's Frank-Walter Steinmeier latest trip to Asia was intended to provide more clarity. Amid a delicate period, Steinmeier sought a balancing act in China between respect and criticism.

According to recent reports, it was a state visit of a kind rarely seen today. For four days, Steinmeier traveled across the country: from Hefei, where the German automaker Volkswagen's China operations are headquartered, through historic villages and the imposing landscapes of the Yellow Mountains. He also visited several points of interest of Chinese history, art, and science, and finally, he headed to Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing's political center.

It has been revealed that steinmeier—who is set to leave office in March 2027— spoke as a statesman and diplomat on matters of German and European interest. Chinese President Xi Jinping and Steinmeier have known each other for many years, so in this respect, the president was the right man to address even the most difficult concerns as a European.

This political balancing act between respect and criticism did not trigger any visible outrage in Beijing.

When he spoke with Chinese leaders about their subsidies for exports to Europe and the related matter of the trade deficit, Xi replied: "I am ready to work together to open a upcoming chapter in the comprehensive strategic partnership between our two countries and to advance the development of global governance.".

Just how much willingness lies behind the push for a strategic partnership will become clear during further negotiations between the EU and China.

Xi Jinping seems to understand that a persistent trade deficit with Europe could also become a problem for his country, as an economic crisis in Europe could further strain China's economy.

Sources indicate that as "the world's second- and third-largest economies," China and Germany also bear "an important responsibility for the development of relations between China and Europe, as well as for stable growth in the global economy," Xi Jinping mentioned. While that may not sound like a breakthrough yet, it certainly sounds like an understanding.

In contrast to his economic arguments, Steinmeier's political appeals for Beijing to assume more responsibility for the international order fell on deaf ears.

According to recent reports, the German president addressed global conflicts and wars on several occasions in Beijing, including Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine. But he received no responses in official statements.

That same evening, the news channel of the Chinese TV network CCTV aired a report that merely covered Steinmeier's visit to a well-known astrophysics institute.

There was no mention of the call for China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, to do more to promote world peace.

Mitat Özdemir is one of more than 870,000 Turkish workers who were recruited to Germany by a government program between 1961 and 1973. He dealt with tough factory work, language barriers and cultural differences.

Industry observers note that six decades later, he and his family still live in Germany. How did the program from back then shape their lives and modern Germany?

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.

North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.

"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he mentioned.

"You can also notice it here at this place, how much a country suffers from division and how strong the desire is for reunification, at least in this part of the Korean Peninsula," he said, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience while visiting Seoul.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state.".

A glass cabinet containing memorabilia linked to the 1958 Munich Air Disaster, in which eight Manchester United footballers lost their lives, was smashed and plundered in the Munich suburb of Trudering this week.

The display case on Manchesterplatz forms part of a memorial commemorating the tragedy which occurred when the United team made a refueling stop in Munich while on the way back from a European Cup game in Belgrade, Serbia, on February 6, 1958.

The plane struggled to take off again in the wintery conditions at the old Munich-Riem airport to the east of the city center and, on the third attempt, ploughed off the end of the runway and into a house. Of the 44 people on board, 23 were killed, including eight United players, several journalists and two crew members.

The crash site has become a place of pilgrimage for United supporters and, in 2020, the cabinet was installed on the initiative of the Red Docs Munich – a local Bayern Munich fan club – to house the various memorabilia and tributes left by visitors.

In a recent development, munich police noted the cabinet was broken into on Monday morning between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (07:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. UTC), with the unknown perpetrators making off with a glass sculpture and several medals.

"They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ifty Ahmed, chairman of the Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF), told the BBC, adding: "Whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories.".

In a recent development, the Red Docs Munich arranged for replacement glass to be installed on the same day. The MMMF stated Manchester United had offered to pay for the repairs but said the foundation had covered the costs itself.

The drop comes amid weak demand in China, and US tariffs.

A ban on new Stolpersteine ("stumbling stones") to commemorate victims of the Holocaust in the eastern German town of Heidenau will be upheld after five petitions against the measure were thrown out.

Local councilors from Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) voted together in September to pass the controversial ban on upcoming stones being laid in the town in Saxony, near Dresden.

Petitions against the measure were submitted from across Germany — as well as one from the Netherlands — calling for victims of the Nazi regime to continue to be remembered in Heidenau by way of the small metal plaques embedded in pavements.

"Not everybody has to like the stumbling stones but everyone should have the possibility to lay one in public," one councilor, Michael Schürer, told Germany's Catholic News Agency (KNA), criticizing the rejection of the petitions.

The initiators of the Heidenau ban had argued that, while remembering Holocaust victims remains essential, the placement of Stolpersteine leads to "passersby walking over or even stepping onto the names of the victims." They suggested honoring victims at a local cemetery instead.

The decision of the local Heidenau CDU to join forces with the AfD to pass the motion sparked a nationwide scandal and furthered the debate over the conservatives' commitment to the political "firewall" against the far right.

"We both bear responsibility for the ⁠international order ​and for the conditions under which states in this world maintain and shape their relations," Steinmeier stated.

President Xi praised what he called an "all-dimensional strategic partnership" between China and Germany, calling for new cooperation based on stability and mutual benefit.

"This newly introduced paradigm sends a positive signal to the world: we favor openness over closure, and cooperation over confrontation," Xi stated during opening remarks, emphasizing the start of a "new chapter" in Germany-China ties.

Xi added that he hopes Germany and the European Union will stick by a "rational, pragmatic and friendly" China policy, adding that cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences in China-EU relations.

The EU has a massive trade deficit with China, which reached €360 billion ($400.4 billion) last year and is set to exceed that level this year.

Recent findings suggest that brussels has accused China of unfair economic practices, saying its state subsidies for its industries are creating an unlevel playing field. Germany with its export based economy, the EU's largest, is hit hard by China's manufacturing surplus flooding global markets.

Industry groups say the surge in imports from China is leading to an increasing number of factory closures in the bloc.

Nonetheless, "differences and problems can always be resolved," the Chinese president stated.

While German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in South Korea on Friday called for a better rule-based trade order, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier was in the Chinese capital in a bid to smooth out trade disagreements.

In Beijing, Steinmeier called for preserving the "win-win principle" characterizing Sino-German relations, borrowing from the expression "win-win cooperation," one of the most frequently used phrases in Chinese foreign policy statements.

Germany's economic ties with China have gone through a shock in recent years, with Chinese manufacturing growing into sectors once dominated by German firms, and Chinese electric cars taking over market share.

At the start of a meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, Steinmeier cited a recent deal limiting exports of Chinese hybrid cars to the EU in exchange for select tariff cuts on EU exports to China as an example of a "a way to find solutions.".

Steinmeier also brought up Germany's growing trade deficit with China, which grew to nearly €90 billion ($100 billion) last year.

Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

Steinmeier noted Germany would work to solve trade problems with China. "We are coming with the intention of maintaining and strengthening the framework for good economic exchange between our two countries," Steinmeier said.

Later in the day, the German president, who occupies a largely ceremonial role without policymaking power, was also recieved by an honor guard alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During his final day of a whirlwind Asia tour this week, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul on Friday that Germany and Europe are ready to cooperate with Asian economies to foster a rules-based economic order.

Merz stated the European Union is ready to take the lead in shaping a better deal for countries in Asia feeling the pressure of a destabilized rules-based trade order.

Sources indicate that "Competition between the US and China is ramping up. Tariffs, technological decoupling strategies and a tough race for critical raw materials and new technologies are fundamentally changing the rules of our global economy," Merz said.

In a recent development, "These conflicts and systemic shifts in power patterns concern us all. They particularly concern economically aspiring partners in the Indo-Pacific, as well as in Germany and in Europe.".

During stops in Singapore and Japan this week, Merz pushed for free trade partnerships and greater European cooperation with Asian economies.

In Singapore on Wednesday, Merz called for a free trade agreement between the EU and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), a sweeping multilateral free trade agreement connecting the Asia Pacific and the Americas.

In a recent development, the UK is the single European signatory, albeit outside of the EU bloc. The US pulled out during the first administration President Donald Trump in 2017, scuttling the original version, the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP).

"We want to offer opportunities beyond bilateral agreements,"he stated in Seoul on Friday.

"We are resolutely joining forces against unilateralism, autocratic power politics and violations of international law," Merz added.

"When supply chains become political pawns, when access to key technologies is obstructed or when efforts to secure raw materials resemble displays of power rather than fair partnerships, this jeopardizes growth, prosperity and ultimately the security of entire regions.".

Merz also tried to allay concerns about EU protectionism under the "Made in Europe" scheme intended to protect carmakers.

"There is a fear that we might be facing ‌a new wave of European protectionism - that we are closing ‌ourselves off from other nations," ‌Merz remarked.

"I take these concerns very seriously. I will carry them back not just to Berlin, ‌but also to Brussels, and I will certainly raise the fact that these concerns were expressed to me quite forcefully here," he added.

Citing Germany as an example, South Korean Prime Minister Han Seong Sook told the conference  "German companies are using Korea as a central hub to expand their presence in the Asia-Pacific region.".

By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 14:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 18:39.

Manchester City’s winless run in the Premier League has been extended to four games after they were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Enzo Maresca’s “main target” was to secure all three points against the Cottagers following a dismal run of three consecutive losses to Aston Villa, Brighton, and Nottingham Forest prior to the international break.

However, the Citizens fell behind inside the opening 16 minutes when Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz – starting his first PL game of the season at the expense of Gonzalo Garcia – curled a sweet strike into the top corner following a sweeping counter-attack.

Erling Haaland thought he had equaliser less than 10 minutes later, but he was controversially deemed to have fouled goalkeeper Bernd Leno before prodding the ball over the line.

Elliot Anderson did restore parity for the hosts, though, with a superbly-struck volley just before the hour mark, but in a second half that saw both teams create decent openings, the visitors admirably held on to claim a share of the spoils, ending an English record 20-game losing streak against the Sky Blues.

The draw represents Man City’s first in the top flight this season and leaves them sitting third in the Premier League table, five points behind leaders Arsenal – who face Newcastle United later tonight – and just behind second-placed Brighton on goal difference, with the Seagulls to take on Hull City on Sunday.

As for Fulham, a third successive draw has seen them extend their unbeaten run in the division to five matches, with Alvaro Arbeloa’s men sitting 14th in the top-flight standings and three points above the relegation zone.

Oliver Thomas live from the Etihad Stadium.

After winning his first seven Premier League games in charge of Man City, a feat no other manager has ever achieved in the division, Enzo Maresca has since seen his team stumble and hand Arsenal a significant title boost even before entering the month of December.

One of the biggest concerns for Maresca is how frail his defence has looked for the majority of this season, with 18 goals conceded across their last nine matches in all competitions, while City have failed to keep a single clean sheet in each of their last seven matches at the Etihad.

Maresca has acknowledged that finding the right balance is key for his new-look Citizens side and it’s ‘normal’ for teams in transition to have moments of struggle, but concerns over his defence, team structure and the performances of individuals are growing heading into a hectic fixture period.

Regardless of the outcome regarding their well-documented guilty verdict appeal, Man City would face an uphill battle to stay in the Premier League title race if they lose at Arsenal next weekend, with a fourth league defeat in five games leaving them trailing the Gunners by a daunting margin before the festive schedule even begins.

As for Fulham, Arbeloa has now steadied the ship following a challenging start to life in Premier League management, with nine of their 11 points accumulated across the last five gameweeks.

The Cottagers are by no means out of trouble just yet, but this positive run of form, extended by a hard-earned point at Man City, has given the club’s supporters genuine hope that a protracted relegation battle can be avoided.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 14:53.

Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Sandro Tonali is missing from Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town due to illness.

The Italy international was a surprise absentee from the Lilywhites' squad against the Tractor Boys, as Conor Gallagher was instead given the nod in central midfield with Mateus Fernandes.

Tonali was not name-checked in De Zerbi's pre-game press conference, and the expectation was that the former Newcastle United man would make his 11th Premier League start of the season.

However, Tonali's perfect starting streak in the top-flight campaign is now over, and De Zerbi explained the midfielder's absence when speaking to reporters ahead of kickoff.

In a recent development, "(The reasons for the changes are) a combination of physical condition (and defeat to Leeds). Many players, they came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days. Rodrigo Bentancur arrived yesterday, just yesterday working with us," De Zerbi said.

"I am lucky because I have a great squad. Many players. All players are very close in level so now we start a very tough period of three games in a row. We are ready.".

De Zerbi made a total of six changes to his starting lineup from the XI that began the 1-0 loss to Ipswich Town before the international break, including a landmark start in attack for Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old makes his full Premier League debut at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of a much-changed attack, which also sees Dominic Solanke and James Maddison replace Omar Marmoush and Archie Gray.

Further back, Destiny Udogie and Marcos Senesi have displaced Andy Robertson and Micky van de Ven, who are on the bench alongside Marmoush, Gray and the returning Savio and Lucas Bergvall.

Tonali has played over 500 more Premier League minutes than Gallagher so far this season, but the England international nevertheless leads his Italian colleague in several per 90 metrics.

As per the comparison chart, Gallagher ranks higher in terms of duels won, tackles and interceptions per 90, as well as winning more free kicks and committing more fouls.

The former Chelsea man also attempts more shots per game and boasts a higher ratio of shots on target, but Tonali triumphs in terms of successful passes, significant chances created and dribble success rate.

However, with a fully-fit Maddison back in the starting lineup, Spurs should have little in the way of creativity concerns as De Zerbi's men bid to return to winning ways on home territory.
